page.overview:
Who is Jorge de Bagration?

Jorge de Bagration y de Mukhrani (February 22 1944 - January 16 2008) was a driver of Spanish citizenship, but was born in Italy, was a claimant to the hereditary throne of the country of Georgia, and a cousin of a claimant to the hereditary throne of Russia.

De Bagration began his motorsport career in 1959, initially with motorcycles, and from 1963, he competed in various car racing series. He made two attempts to enter Formula One; the first was at the 1968 Spanish Grand Prix with a Lola, but his entry was denied.

His second attempt to participate in a Grand Prix also took place in Spain, at the 1974 Spanish Grand Prix. However, his efforts were thwarted by a series of unusual circumstances. He had purchased a Surtees TS16 for the race and was listed on the entry list. Unfortunately, this list was lost when the outgoing president of the Spanish Motor Sport Federation vacated his office. When a new entry list was compiled, due to some sponsorship issues De Bagration was facing, he was left off. Regardless of whether he could have competed with reduced sponsorship, he should have been included on the list of entrants. As a result, his hopes of racing at the highest level of motorsport came to an end.

Later, he shifted his focus to rallying, achieving his best results by winning the Spanish Rally Championship in 1979 and 1981 driving a Lancia Stratos HF. He retired from motorsport in 1982.
